epic.title: [epic] Hotseat UI: play a match through RoundDriver
epic.body:
## Primary Criteria
### Goal

A hotseat scene that lets two human players play a full match against each other through `RoundDriver` — choosing and submitting core actions, passing the Power Step, and watching the round and End Segment advance — instead of a match only being drivable from test code.

### Expected Behavior

- `scenes/main.tscn` stops being a bare `Node` and hosts (or loads) a playable scene wired to `RoundDriver`.
- Each Action Step, the active player (named by `RoundDriver.active_player_id()`) can submit one of the built core actions (Move, Attack, Charge, Guard) against their own fighters, or explicitly decline.
- Each Power Step, both players can pass in turn until the Step closes.
- The UI renders board state (fighter positions, damage, flags) after each submission, from the `TurnResult`/`GameState` handed back — it never reads or mutates `rules/` state directly.
- At the Combat Segment boundary, the scene calls the driver's `end_segment()` and shows the new round's state.
- The loop stops cleanly when `EndSegment` refuses on the final round; what happens then is §11 victory determination (#173), separate work.

### Constraints

- Use existing systems and extension points where appropriate — `RoundDriver` (#185, merged in #201) is the intended integration surface; no new path into `rules/` from the UI.
- Do not add third-party dependencies unless explicitly required.
- Do not modify unrelated systems.
- UI/game-side code only: `scenes/`, `scripts/` (view layer). No change to `rules/`.
- Every submitted command still goes through `RoundDriver` → `Authority`/`ActionRunner` — the scene gathers intent and renders results, it never resolves an action itself. `tests/gate_bypass_contract_test.gd`'s no-receiver-qualified-`.resolve(`-under-`scripts/` constraint applies here too.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Relevant automated tests exist
- [ ] Existing tests pass
- [ ] Godot headless validation passes
- [ ] Two human players can play a full Combat Segment of a round, start to finish, through the scene alone — no script or test driving the sequence
- [ ] Declining a Turn (the default Action Step) is reachable through the UI, not only through `RoundDriver.decline()` in tests
- [ ] The scene never calls `.resolve()` on a `TurnAction` or reaches into `res://rules/` directly

### Out of Scope

- §4 Setup (roster building, deployment, mulligan) — the scene is handed an already-built `GameState`/roster, exactly as `RoundDriver`'s own tests are today. A separate issue if pre-match setup needs its own UI.
- §11 victory determination and §10 step 6's final-round branch (#173) — the loop stops when `EndSegment` refuses on the final round.
- The card system, and any Power Step play beyond passing — no cards exist yet.
- Networking, LAN, or any transport work — hotseat only, one process, two people sharing a keyboard/screen.
- AI opponent.

## Dependencies

| Relationship | Issue | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| None | — | — |

## Supporting Criteria
### Context

Filed as the surviving half of #172 ("Add hotseat game loop to drive matches"). Epic #181 (PR #201) resolved #172's other half — `EndSegment.run()` now has a game-side caller, `scripts/round_driver.gd` — but `RoundDriver` was explicitly scoped as headless and call-driven: its own epic says "this is not a UI Issue and there is still no hotseat interface." This issue is that interface. Extraction plan §5.4's MVP "done" test — "you can play a full 3-round hotseat match end to end" — is still not reachable without it.

#### Scenario: happy_path

1. A dev-authored `GameState` (two players, a small roster each) is loaded into the scene.
2. P1 is shown as active, picks a fighter and an action, and submits it through the scene.
3. Both players pass the Power Step through the scene; the Turn completes and P2 becomes active.
4. Play continues, alternating, through a full round; the scene calls `end_segment()` and shows round 2 with flags cleared.

### Human Validation

- [ ] Gameplay feel — this is the first Issue where a person plays the game rather than a test asserting state, so a manual playthrough matters. (Not checkable in this session: Godot is not installed here.)

## Notes

Related: #172 (the deferred-finding this supersedes for the UI half — worth closing as superseded once this is triaged), #181 / #201 (RoundDriver, the integration surface this builds on), #173 (victory determination, explicitly out of scope here).

## Plan

The UI half of #172 decomposes into four headless game-side classes and one thin scene. The split is forced by the harness: `tests/test_bootstrap.gd` runs synchronous `static func run() -> bool` suites with no scene fixtures, so everything that must be automated lives in `RefCounted` code and the scene stays thin enough to verify by playing it.

- `HexLayout` is the only place a pixel coordinate meets a cube coordinate (guide §4). Pointy-top, drawn with `Node2D._draw()`, no `TileMapLayer`.

Implement only the Scope and Acceptance Criteria below. The parent epic provides context only; it does not expand this task's scope, and neither do sibling tasks.

- broaden this task;

- implement sibling tasks;
- make speculative improvements;

Run `.github/scripts/validate-godot.sh` before reporting completion. The implementation pull request must be titled starting with `[204]` and must close this Issue -- `Closes #204` -- and must not close the parent epic.

---

## Provenance

- Parent epic: #203
- Planner Task: T1

## Model Tier

- Recommended: `opus`

The planner judged this task `opus` work: it fixes the order a whole match is played in, and a wrong derivation here -- a session that pre-gates, auto-passes, or reads the active player off the gate -- is architecture that later work inherits. It is the implementer session's starting model, not a pin: an unavailable model escalates rather than failing the run, and an operator who sets the `IMPLEMENTER_MODELS` repository variable outranks it. Relabel this Issue `model:haiku|sonnet|opus` to overrule it.

## Objective

A headless `HotseatSession` in `scripts/` that answers, for a match in progress, which step of which Turn it is and which player must act next; routes every player command through `RoundDriver`; and reports the Combat Segment boundary and the end of the match. A UI can then be driven entirely by asking it, and a test can play three full rounds without counting a Turn.

## Scope

Add `scripts/hotseat_session.gd` declaring `class_name HotseatSession extends RefCounted`.

Constructed `_init(authority: Authority, templates: FighterTemplates, driver: RoundDriver = null)`, building `RoundDriver.new(authority, templates)` when none is given -- the pattern `RoundDriver._init()` already sets for its optional `ActionRunner`, so the session and the driver can never be a mismatched pair by accident. It holds no `GameState` of its own: the state comes off `Authority.state()` at the point of use, the precedent `ActionRunner` and `RoundDriver` both document at length.

Public surface, and nothing beyond it:

- `enum Phase { ACTION_STEP, POWER_STEP, SEGMENT_COMPLETE, MATCH_COMPLETE }`
- `phase() -> Phase` -- `MATCH_COMPLETE` when `state.combat_segment_complete()` and `state.is_final_round()`; `SEGMENT_COMPLETE` when the Segment is complete and the round is not the final one; `POWER_STEP` when `state.power_step_open`; `ACTION_STEP` otherwise.
- `active_player_id() -> String` -- delegates to `RoundDriver.active_player_id()`.
- `players_to_act() -> Array[String]` -- in `ACTION_STEP`, the active player alone. In `POWER_STEP`, every player in `state.turn_order()` except the last entry of `state.power_step_passes()` when that record is non-empty, ordered so the active player comes first. Empty in `SEGMENT_COMPLETE` and `MATCH_COMPLETE`.
- `player_to_act() -> String` -- the first of `players_to_act()`, or `""`.
- `submit(action: TurnAction, requester_id: String) -> TurnResult`, `decline(player_id: String) -> TurnResult`, `pass_power_step(player_id: String) -> TurnResult` -- one line each, delegating to the identically named `RoundDriver` methods and returning the `TurnResult` unwrapped and unmodified, refusals and failures included.
- `advance_segment() -> TurnResult` -- `RoundDriver.end_segment()`, likewise unwrapped.

Add `tests/hotseat_session_test.gd` (`class_name HotseatSessionTest`, `static func run() -> bool`, with a `static func _expect(condition: bool, message: String) -> Array[String]` helper) covering the criteria below, and register it in `tests/test_bootstrap.gd`'s `_suites`.

## Files or Subsystems Expected to Change

- `scripts/hotseat_session.gd`
- `tests/hotseat_session_test.gd`
- `tests/test_bootstrap.gd`

## Architecture Constraints

- Every player command reaches a resolver through `RoundDriver` -> `ActionRunner`. The session resolves nothing.
- **The session is not a second gate.** It refuses nothing on its own and pre-checks no entitlement: an out-of-phase or out-of-turn command is submitted like any other and comes back refused by `Authority` or failed by the action, and that answer is returned unchanged. Whose question is whose stays as `scripts/authority.gd` documents it.
- `active_player_id()` comes from `RoundDriver`, never from `Authority.active_player_id()`, and the session never calls `Authority.set_active_player()`.
- The session never passes on a player's behalf and never supplies the second pass. Spec §5.3 is explicit that passing is a move, not an absence.
- The session counts nothing -- no Turn counter, no round counter, no pass tally of its own. `phase()` and `players_to_act()` are derived from `GameState` at the moment they are asked, so a state restored by `GameState.from_dict()` reports correctly with no extra work.
- `MATCH_COMPLETE` reports that `EndSegment` would refuse, and nothing more. It is not a victory check: no winner, no score, no §11 branch, not even a partial one.
- `tests/gate_bypass_contract_test.gd` scans `scripts/` for receiver-qualified `.resolve(` and for the literal `res://rules/`. The new file must contain neither and must not be added to its `EXEMPT_FILES`. Naming a `rules/` type by its global `class_name` is explicitly permitted and needs no `preload()`.
- `scripts/round_driver.gd`, `scripts/authority.gd`, `scripts/action_runner.gd` and everything under `rules/` are unchanged by this task. If the session appears to need a new method on one of them, stop and report it rather than adding one.
- `scenes/main.tscn` stays a bare `Node` in this task. The scene is a sibling task.
- Tests are plain GDScript with no framework, per `docs/godot-implementation-guide.md` §7. The suite lives under `tests/`, not `rules/tests/`, because it names game-side types -- the reason `tests/round_driver_test.gd`'s docstring gives. Registering it in `_suites` is required: `tests/orphan_test_contract_test.gd` fails the build on a suite that never runs. Split across a second registered file if it approaches `.gdlintrc`'s 1000-line cap.
- Do not add third-party dependencies or addons.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `phase()` reports `ACTION_STEP` on a freshly built state, `POWER_STEP` after one core action resolves through the session, and `ACTION_STEP` again after both players' passes, with `active_player_id()` having advanced to the next player
- [ ] During an open Power Step `player_to_act()` is the active player before any pass and the opponent after the active player's pass; `players_to_act()` is empty in `SEGMENT_COMPLETE` and in `MATCH_COMPLETE`
- [ ] A suite plays three full rounds end to end -- `turns_per_player` and `rounds_per_match` read off the authored `res://resources/round/round_profile.tres`, neither restated as a literal -- driven only by `phase()` and `player_to_act()`: it never counts Turns, never calls `Authority.set_active_player()`, and finishes with `phase()` reporting `MATCH_COMPLETE`. A bounded loop guard is reported as a failure when reached, never used as the stopping condition.
- [ ] At the end of a non-final round's Combat Segment `phase()` is `SEGMENT_COMPLETE` and `advance_segment()` succeeds, after which `round_number` is one higher, `turns_taken` is 0, no fighter on the board holds a flag in `StatusFlags.round_level()`, and `phase()` is `ACTION_STEP` with the front of the turn order active
- [ ] On the final round `phase()` is `MATCH_COMPLETE` once the Segment completes, and `advance_segment()` returns `EndSegment.FAILURE_FINAL_ROUND` leaving `state.digest()` byte-identical
- [ ] An action submitted through the session by the non-active player comes back carrying `Authority.REFUSED_NOT_YOUR_TURN`, and a second consecutive pass by the same player comes back carrying `PowerStepPassAction.FAILURE_ALREADY_PASSED`; each leaves `state.digest()` unchanged
- [ ] `decline(player_id)` through the session leaves the `"guarded"` flag on the first eligible fighter of that player in `fighter_ids()` order, and that Turn still completes only on its two Power Step passes
- [ ] `HotseatSessionTest` is registered in `tests/test_bootstrap.gd`'s `_suites` and its name appears in the headless run's output
- [ ] `tests/gate_bypass_contract_test.gd` passes with `scripts/hotseat_session.gd` in the tree and no new entry in its `EXEMPT_FILES`

## Out of Scope

- Any scene, node, `Control`, input handling or rendering. This task adds no `Node` subclass.
- Building the starting `GameState` -- a sibling task does that; this suite builds its own fixture the way `tests/round_driver_test.gd` does.
- Constructing `MoveAction`/`AttackAction`/`ChargeAction`/`GuardAction` from player intent -- a sibling task.
- §11 victory determination and §10 step 6's final-round branch (#173). `MATCH_COMPLETE` is where this stops.
- §4 Setup: rosters, deployment, mulligan, decks.
- The card system and any Power Step play beyond passing.
- Networking, LAN, transport, AI opponent.
- A clock, a timer, or a disconnect handler.
- Any change to `rules/`, `scripts/authority.gd`, `scripts/action_runner.gd` or `scripts/round_driver.gd`.

## Dependencies

| Relationship | Issue | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Blocks | #208 | The hotseat scene is driven entirely by this session's reports |

## Provenance

- Parent epic: #203
- Planner Task: T2

## Model Tier

- Recommended: `sonnet`

The planner judged this task `sonnet` work: ordinary implementation against APIs that already exist, with the one real trap -- re-deriving a rule in `scripts/` instead of asking the rules module -- written out as a constraint below. It is the implementer session's starting model, not a pin: an unavailable model escalates rather than failing the run, and an operator who sets the `IMPLEMENTER_MODELS` repository variable outranks it. Relabel this Issue `model:haiku|sonnet|opus` to overrule it.

## Objective

A headless `ActionOptions` in `scripts/` that turns a fighter selection into the affordances a UI can offer -- which of my fighters can act, which hexes they can reach, which enemies they can attack, which hexes they can charge to -- and builds the corresponding `TurnAction`, so the view never assembles a command out of templates and profiles itself and never re-derives a rule to decide what to show.

## Scope

Add `scripts/action_options.gd` declaring `class_name ActionOptions extends RefCounted`, constructed `_init(templates: FighterTemplates, combat_profile: CombatProfile)`. It holds no `GameState`: every method takes the state it is asked about.

Queries:

- `actable_fighters(state: GameState, player_id: String) -> Array[String]` -- that player's fighters, in `state.fighter_ids()` order, that are still the board's occupant of their own recorded position (spec §9's defeat test, as `DefaultActionStep` applies it).
- `move_destinations(state: GameState, fighter_id: String) -> Array[Vector3i]` -- `state.board.reachable_from(position, fighter.move())` with the origin removed; empty when `ChargeLockout.locks_out(state, fighter)`.
- `attack_targets(state: GameState, fighter_id: String) -> Array[String]` -- every other fighter id for which the candidate `AttackAction`'s own `refusal_from(state, attacker_position)` comes back empty; empty when the fighter is held by the Charge lockout.
- `charge_targets(state: GameState, fighter_id: String) -> Array[String]` and `charge_destinations(state: GameState, fighter_id: String, target_id: String) -> Array[Vector3i]` -- the destinations are the move destinations from which the candidate attack half's `refusal_from()` is empty, which is the same question `ChargeAction._refusal()` asks; a charge target is one with at least one such destination.

Builders, each returning `null` when a fighter id is unknown or a template is missing:

- `move(state, fighter_id, destination) -> MoveAction`
- `attack(state, fighter_id, target_id) -> AttackAction`
- `guard(state, fighter_id) -> GuardAction`
- `charge(state, fighter_id, target_id, destination) -> ChargeAction`

Templates come from `FighterTemplates.template_for(state, fighter_id)`; the `CombatProfile` is the one handed in at construction. Add `tests/action_options_test.gd` (`class_name ActionOptionsTest`, `static func run() -> bool`, with a `static func _expect(condition: bool, message: String) -> Array[String]` helper) and register it in `tests/test_bootstrap.gd`'s `_suites`.

## Files or Subsystems Expected to Change

- `scripts/action_options.gd`
- `tests/action_options_test.gd`
- `tests/test_bootstrap.gd`

## Architecture Constraints

- **No rule is re-derived here.** Every query answers by asking the rules module's own predicates -- `Board.reachable_from()`, `AttackAction.refusal_from()`, `ChargeLockout.locks_out()`, `Board.occupant_at()`. Do not write a second range check, a second line-of-sight check, a second reachability search or a second lockout rule in `scripts/`. If a query cannot be answered without one, stop and report it rather than writing the rule twice.
- **Options are an affordance, not permission.** A command built here still goes to `Authority` and still may be refused or fail, and the caller reports that answer. This class is not a pre-gate and must not be described as one.
- It resolves nothing. `tests/gate_bypass_contract_test.gd` scans `scripts/` for receiver-qualified `.resolve(` and for the literal `res://rules/`: the new file must contain neither and must not be added to its `EXEMPT_FILES`. Naming a `rules/` type by its global `class_name` to *construct* a command is explicitly permitted and needs no `preload()`.
- It draws nothing from `state.rng` and mutates no state: every method is a read.
- It loads no resource. The `CombatProfile` is handed in; `FighterTemplates` already knows how to find templates.
- Adding a command is still one new `TurnAction` subclass. This class is a convenience for the view, not a registry or dispatch table the gate reads -- `scripts/authority.gd` and `scripts/action_runner.gd` are unchanged by this task, as is everything under `rules/`.
- Tests are plain GDScript with no framework, under `tests/` (they name game-side types), registered in `_suites` -- `tests/orphan_test_contract_test.gd` fails the build on a suite that never runs. Split across a second registered file if it approaches `.gdlintrc`'s 1000-line cap.
- Do not add third-party dependencies or addons.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `actable_fighters()` returns only the named player's fighters, in `fighter_ids()` order, and omits one whose recorded position the board no longer reports it at
- [ ] `move_destinations()` equals `Board.reachable_from(position, fighter.move())` minus the fighter's own hex, contains no occupied or blocked hex, and is empty for a fighter held by `ChargeLockout.locks_out()`
- [ ] `attack_targets()` omits the fighter itself, a friendly fighter, one out of `range_hexes`, one with no line of sight, and one already defeated; every id it does return builds an `AttackAction` that resolves successfully through an `ActionRunner`
- [ ] Every hex `charge_destinations()` offers builds a `ChargeAction` that resolves successfully through an `ActionRunner`, and `charge_targets()` is empty for a fighter that cannot reach any hex from which its attack half would be legal
- [ ] Each builder returns an action whose `actor_id()` is the fighter asked for, and returns `null` for a fighter id the state does not hold
- [ ] No query mutates the state: `state.digest()` is byte-identical before and after a call to each of the five queries
- [ ] `ActionOptionsTest` is registered in `tests/test_bootstrap.gd`'s `_suites` and its name appears in the headless run's output
- [ ] `tests/gate_bypass_contract_test.gd` passes with `scripts/action_options.gd` in the tree and no new entry in its `EXEMPT_FILES`

## Out of Scope

- Any scene, node, `Control`, input handling or rendering. This task adds no `Node` subclass.
- Submitting anything. The caller submits through `RoundDriver`/`HotseatSession`; this class only builds and queries.
- Turn or step sequencing -- whose Turn it is and which step is open is a sibling task's question.
- Building the starting `GameState` -- a sibling task.
- §6's Focus/Mulligan and any card-driven command. No card system exists.
- Scoring, §11 victory determination, §4 Setup, networking, AI.
- Any change to `rules/`, including adding a query method to a `TurnAction` subclass. If one is genuinely missing, report it.
- Highlighting, colours, or anything about how an option is displayed.

## Provenance

- Parent epic: #203
- Planner Task: T3

## Model Tier

- Recommended: `sonnet`

The planner judged this task `sonnet` work: a fixture built from resources and APIs that already exist, where the judgement needed is about placement and legality rather than about architecture. It is the implementer session's starting model, not a pin: an unavailable model escalates rather than failing the run, and an operator who sets the `IMPLEMENTER_MODELS` repository variable outranks it. Relabel this Issue `model:haiku|sonnet|opus` to overrule it.

## Objective

One game-side entry point that builds a playable starting `GameState` -- a board, two players, a small roster each from the authored fighter templates, and the authored round structure -- so the hotseat scene is handed a match the way `tests/round_driver_test.gd` builds one for itself today, and the fixture lives in exactly one place instead of being retyped per caller.

## Scope

Add `scripts/match_setup.gd` declaring `class_name MatchSetup extends RefCounted`, with static methods only -- the shape `TurnSequence`, `PowerStep`, `EndSegment` and `DefaultActionStep` already use.

- `static func build(match_seed: int = DEFAULT_SEED) -> GameState` -- a hexagonal board of `BOARD_RADIUS` rings, every hex `Board.HexType.NORMAL`; players `"p1"` then `"p2"` added in that order; `turns_per_player` and `rounds_per_match` read off `res://resources/round/round_profile.tres`; two fighters per player built from the authored templates in `res://resources/fighters/` and placed on opposing sides of the board, each also registered as the board's occupant of its hex.
- `static func templates() -> FighterTemplates` -- `FighterTemplates.from_directory()`, so a caller's lookup and the one the state's payloads name are the same set.
- `static func combat_profile() -> CombatProfile` -- `load()` of `res://resources/combat/combat_profile.tres`.
- Named constants for the seed, the board radius, the two player ids and the starting placements, so the fixture is readable and editable in one screen.

Add `tests/match_setup_test.gd` (`class_name MatchSetupTest`, `static func run() -> bool`, with a `static func _expect(condition: bool, message: String) -> Array[String]` helper) and register it in `tests/test_bootstrap.gd`'s `_suites`.

## Files or Subsystems Expected to Change

- `scripts/match_setup.gd`
- `tests/match_setup_test.gd`
- `tests/test_bootstrap.gd`

## Architecture Constraints

- **Authored numbers stay authored.** `turns_per_player`, `rounds_per_match`, the fighter stats and the combat numbers are read from the existing `.tres` files and never restated as literals here or in the suite. The board radius, the seed and the starting hexes are this fixture's own and belong in named constants.
- **No new `Resource` class and no new `.tres` file.** This is a development fixture, not game content: `resources/` is not touched, and `resources/fighters/warrior.tres`, `archer.tres`, `combat/combat_profile.tres` and `round/round_profile.tres` are used as they stand. If the fixture appears to need an authored scenario format, stop and report it rather than inventing one.
- This is §4 Setup's *placeholder*, not §4 Setup. No roster building, no point budget spend, no deployment rules, no mulligan, no roll-off. `ConstructionBudget` is not consulted.
- It builds a state and returns it. It constructs no `Authority`, no `RoundDriver` and no session, resolves nothing, and submits nothing -- `tests/gate_bypass_contract_test.gd` scans `scripts/` for receiver-qualified `.resolve(` and for the literal `res://rules/`; the new file must contain neither and must not be added to its `EXEMPT_FILES`. Loading `res://resources/...` is not a `rules/` path and is fine.
- Determinism is a property of the returned state, not of this class: `build()` draws nothing from the `DeterministicRng` it seeds.
- Placements must be legal by construction -- every starting hex on the board, unoccupied, and no fighter starting adjacent to an enemy, so the opening Turn is a real choice rather than a forced melee.
- Everything under `rules/`, plus `scripts/authority.gd`, `scripts/action_runner.gd` and `scripts/round_driver.gd`, is unchanged by this task.
- `scenes/main.tscn` stays a bare `Node` in this task.
- Tests are plain GDScript with no framework, under `tests/`, registered in `_suites` -- `tests/orphan_test_contract_test.gd` fails the build on a suite that never runs.
- Do not add third-party dependencies or addons.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `build()` returns a state whose `turn_order()` is `["p1", "p2"]` and whose `turns_per_player` and `rounds_per_match` equal the values on `res://resources/round/round_profile.tres`, neither restated as a literal in the suite
- [ ] Every fighter in `fighter_ids()` sits on a hex the board has, is the board's `occupant_at()` that hex, and parses back through `Fighter.from_dict()` against a template registered in `templates()`
- [ ] Each player owns at least two fighters, the two players' fighters are built from different authored templates between them, and no fighter starts adjacent to an enemy fighter
- [ ] `TurnSequence.active_player()` names `"p1"` on the freshly built state, `power_step_open` is false, `turns_taken` is 0 and `round_number` is 1
- [ ] Two `build()` calls with the same seed produce identical `state.digest()`, and two calls with different seeds produce a state whose `rng` differs
- [ ] A full Turn can be played on the built state through `RoundDriver` over `templates()` -- one core action submitted and both Power Step passes -- proving the fixture is playable and its templates match its payloads
- [ ] `MatchSetupTest` is registered in `tests/test_bootstrap.gd`'s `_suites` and its name appears in the headless run's output
- [ ] `tests/gate_bypass_contract_test.gd` passes with `scripts/match_setup.gd` in the tree and no new entry in its `EXEMPT_FILES`
- [ ] `resources/` is unchanged by this task

## Out of Scope

- §4 Setup proper: roster building against `ConstructionBudget`, deployment rules, decks, mulligan, the §5.2 roll-off.
- A save/load path, a scenario file format, or any authored `.tres` for the fixture.
- Any scene, node or UI. This task adds no `Node` subclass.
- Turn sequencing, action construction, rendering -- all sibling tasks.
- Blocked or hazard terrain, feature tokens, the `enhanced` state.
- Scoring, §11 victory determination, networking, AI.
- Any change to `rules/` or to the authored resources.

## Provenance

- Parent epic: #203
- Planner Task: T4

## Model Tier

- Recommended: `sonnet`

The planner judged this task `sonnet` work: the hex layout maths is standard and already sourced, and the view has no decisions in it. It is the implementer session's starting model, not a pin: an unavailable model escalates rather than failing the run, and an operator who sets the `IMPLEMENTER_MODELS` repository variable outranks it. Relabel this Issue `model:haiku|sonnet|opus` to overrule it.

## Objective

A board view that draws a `GameState` -- hexes, fighters, damage, status flags, highlights -- and emits the cube coordinate a player pointed at, plus the pure conversion between cube coordinates and pixels that both directions go through. The view observes and reports a pointer; it decides nothing.

## Scope

Two files of code and one scene.

**`scripts/hex_layout.gd`** -- `class_name HexLayout extends RefCounted`, static methods only, the view boundary `docs/godot-implementation-guide.md` §4 requires:

- `static func to_pixel(coord: Vector3i, size: float) -> Vector2`
- `static func from_pixel(point: Vector2, size: float) -> Vector3i`, rounding through `HexCoord.cube_round()`
- `static func corners(size: float) -> PackedVector2Array` -- the six corner offsets of one hex, for drawing.

Pointy-top orientation, the standard Red Blob Games layout over the cube coordinates `rules/board/hex_coord.gd` already uses. Do not re-derive the algorithms and do not reopen the cube-coordinate choice.

**`scripts/board_view.gd`** -- `class_name BoardView extends Node2D`, attached to **`scenes/board_view.tscn`**:

- `func render(state: GameState, templates: FighterTemplates) -> void` -- stores what it needs and calls `queue_redraw()`.
- `func set_highlights(coords: Array[Vector3i]) -> void` and `func clear_highlights() -> void`.
- `signal hex_selected(coord: Vector3i)`.
- `_draw()` paints every hex in `state.board.coords()` from `Board.hex_type()`, tints the highlight set differently, and for each fighter that is the board's occupant of its own recorded position draws an owner-coloured marker with its id, its `damage_counter()` against `health()`, and its status flags. A fighter the board no longer reports at its position is spec §9's defeated and is not drawn.
- `_unhandled_input()` converts a pressed `InputEventMouseButton` or `InputEventScreenTouch` position into a cube coordinate through `HexLayout.from_pixel()` and emits `hex_selected` only when `state.board.has_hex()` is true for it.

Add `tests/hex_layout_test.gd` (`class_name HexLayoutTest`, `static func run() -> bool`, with a `static func _expect(condition: bool, message: String) -> Array[String]` helper) and register it in `tests/test_bootstrap.gd`'s `_suites`.

## Files or Subsystems Expected to Change

- `scripts/hex_layout.gd`
- `scripts/board_view.gd`
- `scenes/board_view.tscn`
- `tests/hex_layout_test.gd`
- `tests/test_bootstrap.gd`

## Architecture Constraints

- **`HexLayout` is the only place a pixel coordinate meets a cube coordinate.** No conversion is inlined in `board_view.gd`, and no pixel or offset coordinate is ever passed into anything under `rules/` -- guide §4 names mixing the two the most common source of hex bugs.
- **The view decides nothing.** It builds no `TurnAction`, submits nothing, calls nothing on `Authority`, `ActionRunner`, `RoundDriver` or a session, and mutates no `GameState`. It renders what it is handed and emits the hex that was pointed at; what that means is the match scene's question.
- `tests/gate_bypass_contract_test.gd` scans `scripts/` **and `scenes/`** for receiver-qualified `.resolve(` and for the literal `res://rules/` -- including `[ext_resource]` lines, so `scenes/board_view.tscn` must not attach or reference a script from `res://rules/`. Neither new file may be added to its `EXEMPT_FILES`. Naming a `rules/` type by its global `class_name` is permitted and needs no `preload()`.
- Drawn with `Node2D._draw()`, not `TileMapLayer`: no tileset to author, and the hex geometry stays in `HexLayout` where it is testable. Use `ThemeDB.fallback_font` for any drawn text rather than adding a font resource.
- Pointer selection uses the input event directly, not a named Input Map action -- it is a tap or a click at a position, not a key -- and `project.godot` is not edited. Never assume a hover state or a cursor: touch has neither.
- No `_process`, no `_physics_process`, no tweens, no animation, no `CharacterBody`, no collision. A redraw happens because `render()` was called.
- The scene must boot headless without error: `.github/scripts/validate-godot.sh` runs an import pass and a headless boot, and the board view's centring offset lives on the node's own transform rather than inside `HexLayout`.
- `HexLayoutTest` is the automated coverage here. `BoardView` is a `Node` and this repository's harness has no scene fixtures (guide §7), so its verification is the headless boot plus a manual look; do not add a test framework for it, and do not move drawing logic into `HexLayout` to make it testable.
- Everything under `rules/`, and `scripts/authority.gd`, `scripts/action_runner.gd`, `scripts/round_driver.gd`, is unchanged by this task.
- `scenes/main.tscn` stays a bare `Node` in this task. Wiring the board view into the match is a sibling task.
- Do not add third-party dependencies or addons.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `HexLayout.from_pixel(HexLayout.to_pixel(c, size), size) == c` for every cube coordinate of a radius-4 hexagonal board, at more than one `size`
- [ ] `to_pixel(Vector3i(0, 0, 0), size)` is `Vector2.ZERO`, and two coordinates that `HexCoord.are_adjacent()` map to pixel points whose distance is the expected one-hex spacing for that `size`
- [ ] A pixel point sampled anywhere inside a hex's drawn outline rounds back to that hex, including points near its corners
- [ ] `corners()` returns six offsets whose distance from the origin is `size`
- [ ] `BoardView.render()` draws one hex per entry in `state.board.coords()`, an owner-distinguished marker for every fighter that is the board's occupant of its own recorded position, and no marker for one that is not
- [ ] A fighter's drawn marker shows its damage counter against its health and its status flags, so `"guarded"`, `"moved"` and `"charged"` are visible without reading the log
- [ ] `set_highlights()` visibly distinguishes the given hexes and `clear_highlights()` restores them, without either touching the `GameState`
- [ ] Pressing a pointer over a hex on the board emits `hex_selected` once with that hex's cube coordinate; pressing outside the board emits nothing
- [ ] `HexLayoutTest` is registered in `tests/test_bootstrap.gd`'s `_suites` and its name appears in the headless run's output
- [ ] `tests/gate_bypass_contract_test.gd` passes with the two new scripts and `scenes/board_view.tscn` in the tree and no new entry in its `EXEMPT_FILES`
- [ ] `project.godot` and `scenes/main.tscn` are unchanged by this task

## Out of Scope

- The match scene, the HUD, action buttons, the result log, turn sequencing -- sibling tasks.
- Building or submitting any `TurnAction`.
- Animation, tweening, camera control, zoom, pan, sprites, art assets, sound.
- A `TileSet`, a `TileMapLayer`, a theme resource or a font resource.
- Offset-coordinate support of any kind. Cube in, pixels out.
- Range, line-of-sight or reachability computation -- the view is handed a highlight set, it does not work one out.
- §11 victory determination, §4 Setup, cards, networking, AI.
- Any change to `rules/`.

| Relationship | Issue | Why |

| Blocks | #208 | The hotseat scene instances this scene and renders through it |

Run it locally with `/execute-task 208` in Claude Code. Or start a Copilot agent session -- mobile or desktop -- and paste this as the task description:

## Implementation Agent Contract

The full contract is *Executing an Implementation Task* in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, which you are already reading whether you loaded a profile or not. This is its short form.

Implement only the Scope and Acceptance Criteria below. The parent epic provides context only; it does not expand this task's scope, and neither do sibling tasks.

Do not:

- broaden this task;
- redesign architecture;
- implement sibling tasks;

If additional work is discovered, report it under `Discovered out-of-scope work` rather than implementing it.

Run `.github/scripts/validate-godot.sh` before reporting completion. The implementation pull request must be titled starting with `[208]` and must close this Issue -- `Closes #208` -- and must not close the parent epic.

---

## Provenance

- Parent epic: #203
- Planner Task: T5

## Model Tier

- Recommended: `opus`

The planner judged this task `opus` work: it is the integration where the second architectural commitment is easiest to break quietly -- a scene that assembles a command itself, keeps its own copy of the state, or suppresses a refusal would still look like it works. It is the implementer session's starting model, not a pin: an unavailable model escalates rather than failing the run, and an operator who sets the `IMPLEMENTER_MODELS` repository variable outranks it. Relabel this Issue `model:haiku|sonnet|opus` to overrule it.

## Objective

`scenes/main.tscn` stops being a bare `Node` and becomes the hotseat match: two people sharing one screen pick fighters and actions, decline a Turn, pass the Power Step, watch the board and the result log update after every submission, and carry the match across the Segment boundary into the next round -- every command going out through `HotseatSession` -> `RoundDriver` -> `Authority`/`ActionRunner`.

## Scope

`scenes/main.tscn` becomes the match scene itself rather than loading a second one: its root is a `Node` with `scripts/hotseat_match.gd` attached (`class_name HotseatMatch extends Node`), and it instances `scenes/board_view.tscn` plus a `Control` HUD as children. `project.godot`'s `run/main_scene` already points at it and is not edited.

On `_ready()` the scene builds the match once: `MatchSetup.build()`, an `Authority` over that state, a `HotseatSession` over that `Authority` and `MatchSetup.templates()`, and an `ActionOptions` over the same templates and `MatchSetup.combat_profile()`. It keeps the `Authority` as its route to the `GameState` it renders.

The HUD shows, and re-renders after every submission: the round number, the phase from `HotseatSession.phase()`, the player named by `player_to_act()`, the selected fighter, buttons for Move / Attack / Charge / Guard, a Decline button, a Pass button during the Power Step naming the player whose pass it is, a "begin next round" button when the phase is `SEGMENT_COMPLETE`, and a scrolling result log.

The flow, stated so it is not redesigned: select a fighter (by tapping its hex, or from a list of `ActionOptions.actable_fighters()`) -> press an action button -> Guard submits at once; Move and Attack and Charge highlight the relevant hexes or targets from `ActionOptions` and submit when the player taps one; Charge takes two taps, target then destination. Decline and Pass submit immediately for the player named by `player_to_act()`.

Every one of those paths goes through a public intent method on `HotseatMatch`, which is what the buttons' `pressed` signals and `BoardView.hex_selected` are connected to, and what the suite drives:

- `select_fighter(fighter_id: String) -> void`
- `choose_action(kind: StringName) -> void`, with `ACTION_MOVE`, `ACTION_ATTACK`, `ACTION_CHARGE`, `ACTION_GUARD` constants on this class
- `select_hex(coord: Vector3i) -> TurnResult` -- `null` when the tap only advanced the selection, the submitted result when it completed a command
- `decline_turn() -> TurnResult`
- `pass_power_step() -> TurnResult`
- `advance_segment() -> TurnResult`
- `log_lines() -> Array[String]`

At `MATCH_COMPLETE` the scene stops offering commands and says the match is over and that working out who won is #173. It names no winner.

Add `tests/hotseat_match_test.gd` (`class_name HotseatMatchTest`, `static func run() -> bool`, with a `static func _expect(condition: bool, message: String) -> Array[String]` helper), registered in `tests/test_bootstrap.gd`'s `_suites`, which instantiates `res://scenes/main.tscn`, adds it to `(Engine.get_main_loop() as SceneTree).root` so `_ready()` runs, drives the intent methods above, asserts against `HotseatSession` and the log, and frees the node before returning.

## Files or Subsystems Expected to Change

- `scenes/main.tscn`
- `scripts/hotseat_match.gd`
- `tests/hotseat_match_test.gd`
- `tests/test_bootstrap.gd`

## Architecture Constraints

- **Every command goes out through `HotseatSession`.** The scene resolves nothing, builds no action by hand, and never calls `Authority`, `ActionRunner` or `RoundDriver` to submit. `tests/gate_bypass_contract_test.gd` scans `scripts/` and `scenes/` for receiver-qualified `.resolve(` and for the literal `res://rules/` -- including `[ext_resource]` lines in `.tscn` -- and neither new file may be added to its `EXEMPT_FILES`. Naming a `rules/` type by its global `class_name` to read a `TurnResult` is permitted.
- **The scene holds no rule and no derived tally.** Whose Turn, which step, who passes next and whether the Segment is over all come from `HotseatSession`; what a fighter may do comes from `ActionOptions`. The scene adds no turn counter, no pass counter, no legality check of its own, and never calls `Authority.set_active_player()`.
- **An offered option is not a promise.** A submission that comes back refused or failed is reported in the log by its `TurnResult.reason` verbatim and leaves the selection recoverable; the scene does not suppress, translate away or retry it, and does not pre-filter to make refusals impossible.
- **Decline is a first-class button, not a fallback.** Spec §5.3's one explicit way not to choose must be reachable on every Action Step without first selecting a fighter.
- The scene mutates no `GameState`. It re-reads `Authority.state()` after each submission and re-renders; it keeps no copy.
- No autoload is added, and no event bus. Guide §6: the authority/session object is owned by the match scene, and the autoload count stays where it is.
- `scenes/main.tscn` is the only scene whose role changes. `scenes/board_view.tscn` is instanced as authored and its script is not edited; `scripts/hotseat_session.gd`, `scripts/action_options.gd`, `scripts/match_setup.gd`, `scripts/round_driver.gd`, `scripts/authority.gd`, `scripts/action_runner.gd` and everything under `rules/` are unchanged. If one of them appears to be missing something this scene needs, stop and report it.
- Keyboard shortcuts are not required; pointer and buttons are the input surface, and `project.godot`'s Input Map is not edited.
- The scene must boot cleanly headless -- `.github/scripts/validate-godot.sh` boots the main scene with no display server -- and must not require input to reach a rendered first frame.
- Tests are plain GDScript with no framework, under `tests/`, registered in `_suites`. If driving the scene inside the headless harness proves genuinely unworkable, stop and report that rather than deleting the criterion, weakening another suite, or adding a test framework.
- Do not add third-party dependencies or addons.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `scenes/main.tscn` boots to a rendered board with the round number, the phase, and the player who must act shown, having built its match through `MatchSetup` in `_ready()`
- [ ] Two human players can play a full Combat Segment of a round start to finish through the scene alone -- every Turn's Action Step and both Power Step passes -- with no script or test driving the sequence
- [ ] Each of Move, Attack, Charge and Guard is submittable from the HUD for a fighter the active player owns, and the board re-renders from the state handed back afterwards
- [ ] Declining a Turn is reachable from the HUD on every Action Step, without selecting a fighter first, and produces the same result `HotseatSession.decline()` does
- [ ] During an open Power Step the Pass button names the player `HotseatSession.player_to_act()` reports, and the Turn completes only after both players have pressed it in turn
- [ ] A refused or failed submission -- the wrong player acting, an out-of-range attack, a fighter held by the Charge lockout -- appends a log line carrying the `TurnResult.reason` verbatim, changes no board state, and leaves the scene usable
- [ ] When the Combat Segment completes the scene offers the next round rather than advancing itself, and taking it shows round 2 with flags cleared and the front of the turn order active
- [ ] On the final round the scene reports the match over, offers no further command, names no winner, and points at #173
- [ ] `tests/hotseat_match_test.gd` instantiates `res://scenes/main.tscn` under the running `SceneTree`, plays at least one complete Turn through the intent methods -- a submitted action and both passes -- asserts the phase and active player moved as `HotseatSession` reports them and that the log recorded each result, and frees the node
- [ ] `HotseatMatchTest` is registered in `tests/test_bootstrap.gd`'s `_suites` and its name appears in the headless run's output
- [ ] `tests/gate_bypass_contract_test.gd` passes with `scripts/hotseat_match.gd` and the rewritten `scenes/main.tscn` in the tree and no new entry in its `EXEMPT_FILES`
- [ ] `project.godot` and everything under `rules/` are unchanged by this task

## Out of Scope

- §11 victory determination and §10 step 6's final-round branch (#173). The scene stops when `EndSegment` refuses; do not build a partial victory check, a score display or a winner banner.
- §4 Setup: roster building, deployment, mulligan, decks, the §5.2 roll-off. The scene is handed a built state.
- The card system and any Power Step play beyond passing.
- Networking, LAN, transport, spectating, an AI opponent.
- Undo, replay, save/load, a match log file, a seed entry field.
- Animation, tweening, camera pan or zoom, art assets, sound, theming beyond what the HUD needs to be legible.
- A settings screen, a main menu, a pause menu, a quit confirmation.
- Editing `scripts/board_view.gd`, `scripts/hex_layout.gd`, `scripts/hotseat_session.gd`, `scripts/action_options.gd` or `scripts/match_setup.gd` to suit the scene. Report the gap instead.
- Any change to `rules/`, `scripts/authority.gd`, `scripts/action_runner.gd` or `scripts/round_driver.gd`.

## Dependencies

| Relationship | Issue | Why |
